Body:
> AI code review — automated review for reference, author can ignore or act on any point.

Correct and well-scoped fix. In `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts` (hunk `@@ -1110,7`, changed lines ~1113–1118), filtering with `pickBy` before mapping eliminates the `[0].id` TypeError on zero-model providers while leaving the live provider map untouched for the picker — the right layering. The regression tests in `packages/opencode/test/provider/default-model-ids.test.ts` cover the happy path, mixed, and all-empty cases, which matches the failure mode described in issue #44088.

Two considerations:

1. Behavioral change worth confirming downstream: callers previously got a key per provider and now get fewer keys. If `/config/providers` consumers use `defaultModelIDs()[id] === undefined` as "hide this provider," a bare gateway provider will disappear from pickers entirely rather than appearing without a default. If the intent is only crash-proofing, consider keeping keys with `undefined` values or double-checking how `ProviderHttpApi.list` renders empty-model entries.
2. Defensive nit: `Object.keys(item.models)` still throws if `models` is explicitly `undefined` on a hand-built object; `Object.keys(item.models ?? {})` costs nothing given the function's generic contract already admits partial shapes via test casts.

Otherwise clean — minimal diff, clear comment, real regression coverage.

Additional Windows V2 reproduction, now on the newer embedded Bun 1.4.0 runtime.

## Environment

- OpenCode: `opencode2 v0.0.0-beta-17963` (beta channel)
- OS: Windows 11 x64, build `10.0.26200.9168`
- Terminal: Windows Terminal (`TERM=xterm-256color`)
- Shell: PowerShell 7.6.5
- Active plugins: none found in workspace/global config or local plugin directories

## Frequency and process boundary

Four TUI/client exits were observed during one active agent session at `10:01:33Z`, `10:02:04Z`, `10:03:16Z`, and `10:30:31Z` on 2026-08-23. Only the fourth retained the decoded `bun.report` stack below.

The shared OpenCode service did not crash. After the fourth exit, `opencode2 service status` still returned the same server at PID `17616`, and `opencode2 api get /api/health` returned:

```json
{"healthy":true,"version":"0.0.0-beta-17963","pid":17616}
```

The server log records the client event stream ending as:

```text
InterruptError: All fibers interrupted without error
http.method=GET http.url=/api/event http.status=200
```

The server continued handling work and accepted a replacement TUI client. No fatal OpenCode log entry, Windows Error Reporting entry, dump, or temporary Bun artifact was created.

## Decoded Bun crash report

```text
Bun v1.4.0 (34cbb9a) on windows x86_64 [StandaloneExecutable]

Segmentation fault at address 0x1E014680008

- 6 unknown/js code
- vmEntryToJavaScript

Features: standalone_executable, Bun.stderr, Bun.stdin, Bun.stdout, fetch, jsc
```

This confirms a native Bun/JavaScriptCore failure in the TUI client and shows that this Windows V2 crash family persists after the embedded runtime moved from Bun 1.3.14 to 1.4.0.

It does not positively match the older FFI console-guard signature in #31144: this report does not name `JSFFIFunction::trampoline`, and `bun:ffi` is absent from its feature list. The trace is too short to identify the faulty operation because Bun's Windows stack walker currently loses frames around LLInt/`vmEntry*`; the relevant open Bun fixes are oven-sh/bun#38789 and oven-sh/bun#39101. Therefore `vmEntryToJavaScript` should be treated as the last visible boundary frame, not as a proven root cause.

Thanks for the review. Confirming that the full fallback for an overlap cluster is intentional. Overlapping persisted ranges indicate ambiguous or stale metadata, so the renderer avoids arbitrarily choosing a subset to style inline; every mention involved in the conflict remains visible as a badge instead. This also keeps the behavior deterministic for transitive three-way overlap clusters.

The non-null assertion is guarded by the preceding validation as noted. Since there are no blocking issues, I’ll leave the implementation unchanged.

I have a possibly related but distinct case. Same machine, same public IP, same API key, same opencode version (1.18.18), but:

Windows build: works fine
WSL Linux build: intermittent AI_APICallError: Forbidden
Environment
WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04 (kernel 6.18.33.2) + Windows 10
Public IP: 101.87.170.107 (confirmed identical for both)
Provider: opencode-go (Go plan)
OpenCode: 1.18.18 on both sides
Evidence
140 Forbidden errors in one day on WSL
Affected models: deepseek-v4-flash (36), deepseek-v4-pro (18), deepseek-v4-flash-free (16), ox-alpha-free (3), big-pickle (2)
Both opencode-go (57 errors) and opencode (20 errors) providers affected
models.opencode.ai/api.json also returned 403 intermittently from WSL
All endpoints are reachable from WSL (curl works)
Key observation
Since the public IP and API key are identical, this suggests the Forbidden may be related to something the Linux binary sends differently — possibly TLS fingerprint, User-Agent, or other HTTP headers that differ between the Windows and Linux builds.

The error is intermittent on WSL — sometimes the same model works, sometimes it returns Forbidden.

Hi! We independently opened #44389 (explicit opt-in plugin reload) before finding this one — closing it in favor of this broader request.

Offering our plugin-specific findings to fold in here, from reading the current `dev` source:

- **Recovery is blocked, not just iteration**: `packages/opencode/src/plugin/loader.ts` notes Bun caches failed dynamic imports for the process lifetime, so even fixing a broken plugin requires a full restart.
- **Session semantics are worth specifying up front**: registered hooks live in an array captured by the plugin subsystem (`packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts`). An atomic swap gives clean semantics: sessions started after reload observe the new version; already-running sessions keep their current hooks and toolset (documented, intentional).
- **npm-installed plugins sit outside any watcher's reach** (`~/.cache/opencode/packages/<pkg>/`), so an explicit trigger (`opencode plugin reload [spec]`, plus `POST /plugin/reload` for UIs) complements the watching approach discussed in #34492 rather than competing with it.
- Re-running the existing resolve -> entry -> compatibility pipeline keeps the npm version gate active on every reload.

Happy to take the plugin slice of this behind a design review if useful.

Thanks — went through all four against the code. Two landed, two didn't. Pushed the fixes.

**3 (negative `size`) — confirmed, fixed.** `tiers: [{ input: 99, output: 99, tier: { type: "context", size: -1 } }]` billed **108.9** instead of the base **4.5**: the tier matched every context and won. Now dropped. Worth noting `>= 0` isn't enough — `size: 0` still matches every non-zero context, so the guard is `size > 0`.

**Also fixed, which nobody flagged:** my own guard regressed numeric strings. The comparison it replaced coerced `contextTokens > "5000"`, so `Number.isFinite("5000")` silently disabled a tier that used to apply. `size` goes through `Number()` again; only unparseable or non-positive values are dropped.

**1 (tier without pricing) — the mechanism doesn't hold, but there is a real issue underneath.** No NaN: `finite(costInfo?.input ?? 0)` from #43248 turns the missing rates into 0, so that case returns `cost = 0`, `isNaN = false`. What does happen is that such a tier wins the selection and the cost silently drops to 0 instead of the base 4.5. That's preexistent — the old filter selected it too — and fixing it means deciding a policy (drop the tier vs. fall back to base rates), so I left it out of a PR that's about the crash. Happy to add `Number.isFinite(item.input) && Number.isFinite(item.output)` here if you'd rather it land in one go, or file it separately.

**2 (silent drop) — agreed in principle, not here.** `getUsage` is per-turn and logs nothing today, so a warn would be recurring noise. The right place is the boundary: `cost()` in `provider/provider.ts` copies `tier: item.tier` from the models.dev payload with no guard at all, unlike `input`/`output`/`cache`. Happy to open an issue for that.

**4 (b) — already covered.** `"uses matching context cost tier before over-200k fallback"` (compaction.test.ts) uses context 650_000 where **both** the 200k and 500k tiers match, and asserts `2.75 + 0.6 + 0.05`, which only holds if the 500k one wins. New data points suggesting this issue's root-cause analysis is a misdiagnosis.

Tested on Linux with opencode 1.18.21 (@opentui/core 0.4.5) + WezTerm, default `input_newline` keybinds: **Ctrl+Enter newline works both with `enable_kitty_keyboard = false` and `true`.**

The JS method `enableKittyKeyboard()` is indeed dead code, but that's not the negotiation path. In opentui's native code (`packages/core/src/zig/terminal.zig`), `enableDetectedFeatures()` runs after capability detection (called from `renderer.zig`). I captured opencode's actual output inside WezTerm (kitty keyboard enabled): it sends `ESC [?u` (kitty query) and `ESC [>4;1m` (modifyOtherKeys fallback), and once WezTerm answers the query it sends `ESC [>4;0m` + `ESC [>5u` — the kitty flags push — and pops with `ESC [<u` on exit. So the protocol IS negotiated, via the native layer; the JS-level search just missed it.

This native negotiation has existed since Nov 2025 (opentui PRs #251, #259, #298) and was already present in opencode 1.18.3, which bundles @opentui/core 0.4.3. So whatever caused the failure on the reporter's setup (e.g. the terminal or a multiplexer not answering the kitty query, or a capability-detection timing issue), the mechanism described in this issue is not it. Suggest re-testing on the latest release.

The ask in this thread — semantic search across message history — has no substrate to run on today: transcript storage is keyed by id, no content index of any kind (no FTS/vector table anywhere in `packages/core`).

Checked on current `dev`: persistence is now event-sourced SQLite (`<data>/opencode.db`, bun:sqlite — `packages/core/src/database/database.ts`). Messages/parts are projections (`MessageTable`/`PartTable`, `packages/core/src/session/sql.ts`) kept current by a projector subscribed to durable `MessageUpdated`/`PartUpdated` events published from `Session.updatePart`.

That makes an opt-in **local embedding index** incremental and fully off the hot path:

- Background embedder subscribes to post-commit durable events — zero changes to turn handling
- Rebuild/backfill = replay durable events or scan `PartTable`; deletion parity already mirrored by the projector
- One deterministic anchor chunk per session (title + compaction summaries) sits on top of per-part chunks, so aggregate questions get a high-precision entry point; a hierarchical/graph index over that substrate is a natural follow-up
- Provider pluggable, local-first by default (no network, data stays on device); API providers via existing config
- Gated behind `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_*`, following existing precedent

Why core rather than a plugin: plugins can't subscribe to internal EventV2 durable events (server SSE only), so incremental indexing needs core access.

Positioning vs prior art: #20322/#39772 target native auto-memory/learning; this is mechanical retrieval over the same substrate — different consumer, complementary. Cross-project/cross-session recall comes almost free once indexing exists, detail dropped by compaction (#40614) stays queryable, and subagents get fast lookup without extra model calls.

Out of scope: replacing compaction, remote sync, auto-injecting recalled context into prompts.

I have a working POC on this exact design (verified end-to-end: live incremental indexing, cross-session recall through the tool, deletion parity, clean rebuild on restart). Happy to open a draft PR behind the flag — would that be a useful next step here?
